title: Shared Data and Race Conditions knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Shared Data and Race Conditions” in the supplied Java curriculum?
options: Why results may vary across executions
questions.explanation: The supplied PDF lists “Shared mutable state” under lesson 235, “Shared Data and Race Conditions”.

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with shared data and race conditions?
options: Define synchronization or task ownership, cancellation, timeouts, and shutdown behavior explicitly.
Assume the first successful run proves the code is correct.
Change several unrelated parts until the output looks plausible.
Ignore runtime/version requirements if the code looks familiar.
questions.answer_key: Define synchronization or task ownership, cancellation, timeouts, and shutdown behavior explicitly.
questions.explanation: Define synchronization or task ownership, cancellation, timeouts, and shutdown behavior explicitly. A small reproducible test provides stronger evidence than assumption or trial-and-error changes.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest first step when checking an example related to shared data and race conditions?
options: State the expected behavior, run or inspect the smallest relevant example, then test one boundary or failure case.
Skip reproducing the behavior and change multiple settings at once.
Trust a screenshot without checking the program or version that produced it.
Disable all validation and error handling.
questions.answer_key: State the expected behavior, run or inspect the smallest relevant example, then test one boundary or failure case.
questions.explanation: State the expected behavior, run or inspect the smallest relevant example, then test one boundary or failure case. This approach makes the result repeatable and helps isolate the cause of a mismatch.
